Tree concepts

Shapes (per wood type)

quarter — the faceted trunk piece, facedir 0..3 (inner corner = trunk axis at +x +z for 0). Four make a 2×2 trunk, they round the corners of a 3×3. Four facets stepping out, the outermost half width so the neighbour completes it:
{-8,-8, 4, 8,8, 8}
{-6,-8,-1, 8,8, 4}
{-1,-8,-6, 8,8,-1}
{ 4,-8,-8, 8,8,-6}

branch — connected node box, 10/16 thick: core {-5,-5,-5,5,5,5}, arm e.g. right {5,-5,-5,8,5,5}, one arm per face neighbour that is wood.

twig — the same at 6/16: core {-3,-3,-3,3,3,3}, arm right {3,-3,-3,8,3,3}.

The plain log cube (existing) fills trunk interiors and is the first piece of the thickest limbs. Branch, twig and log take facedir only for the bark: param2 0 / 4 / 12 = grain along y / z / x (connected boxes never turn, their tiles do). Leaves are the existing full cubes. Boxes in sixteenths: x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2.

Drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, wheel to zoom. Counts: wood = log + quarter + branch + twig; shape nodes = quarter + branch + twig. “today” = the current schematic (probabilistic nodes counted as present).
